# Political and legal risk

Risk to a foreign owner's title, income and exit. Sources in
[citations.md](../citations.md).

## Read this first: the dimension lost its primary source

**Every US State Department Investment Climate Statement fetched in this run
returned no content.** Ten files across the 2019, 2022, 2024 and 2025 editions
for Costa Rica, Mexico and Panama all recorded HTTP 200 with the body "We're
sorry, this site is currently experiencing technical difficulties… Exception:
forbidden", and the Panama PDF failed to parse [63].

The ICS carries standing sections on Expropriation and Compensation, Dispute
Settlement, and Transfer Policies. Losing all of them means:

- **No expropriation record for any of the nine countries.**
- **No investor-state case count for any of the nine.**
- **No capital-control or repatriation evidence for any of the nine** — the IMF
  AREAER, the authoritative register, also refused this run [65].
- **No investment-treaty recourse evidence.** No fetched file establishes BIT,
  CAFTA-DR or USMCA coverage for a US investor anywhere.

Those four gaps are not closable from this corpus, and no substitute was invented
for them. What follows is what did survive.

## Judicial capacity — the one comparable instrument

The 2025 EU Justice Scoreboard [33] covers six of the nine. Its numeric values
are images that did not survive PDF extraction, so **only rank orders are
reported here**, out of 27 member states:

| Measure | FR | ES | IT | PT | EL | HU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Companies confident investments are protected by law and courts | **10** | 18 | 15 | 20 | **26** | 19 |
| Public perceiving courts as independent | 16 | 21 | 17 | 14 | 23 | 22 |
| Companies perceiving courts as independent | 14 | 21 | 17 | **24** | 16 | 22 |
| Disposition time, civil/commercial, all instances, 2023 | 21 | 24 | **27** | 12 | 26 | **1** |

Two patterns worth naming. **Hungary is the EU's fastest civil justice system on
disposition time and 22nd of 27 on perceived independence** — speed and
independence diverge sharply, and an investor should not read the first as
reassurance about the second. **Portugal ranks 14th on public perception but 24th
on company perception**, the widest public/business gap of the six.

Country-specific recommendations, from the Scoreboard's own footnote 61 [33]: of
the nine, **Hungary alone carries a live rule-of-law recommendation**, and
**Spain is newly flagged for judicial efficiency** in the Commission's June 2025
draft.

The 2024 factsheet supplies actual day counts — see
[tenancy-law.md](tenancy-law.md), where the extraction caveat is set out.

Costa Rica, Mexico and Panama are outside this instrument, and the World Justice
Project index that would have covered them returned empty bodies [65].

## Tenure that is not fee simple

The clearest title risks in this study are structural and statutory, not
political.

**Mexico** [5][6]. Restricted-zone residential property is held through a bank
trust that confers use and enjoyment "**sin constituir derechos reales sobre
ellos**" — expressly no rights in rem. Maximum 50 years, "podrá prorrogarse a
solicitud del interesado" — permissive, not guaranteed. SRE decides "considerando
el beneficio económico y social… para la Nación", may verify compliance "en
cualquier tiempo", and may revoke authorisations. Simulated acts to circumvent
carry a fine **up to the full transaction value**.

**Costa Rica** [7]. The 200 m coastal zone is "parte del patrimonio nacional…
**inalienable e imprescriptible**", so no adverse possession runs against the
State there. Only concessions exist, 5 to 20 years, and renewal "podrá[n]
denegar" for public utility, general convenience, or urban and tourism
development plans. On extinction for reasons attributable to the concessionaire,
improvements and buildings pass to the municipality "**sin que ésta deba
reconocer suma alguna**" — without compensation.

**Panama** [36]. Residential possession recovery runs through a ministry
directorate at first and second instance rather than the ordinary courts, leases
are registered with the ministry, and security deposits are consigned to it.
Not a title risk as such, but a materially different enforcement architecture
from the US. Panama's possessory-rights regime — the well-known distinction
between registered title and *derechos posesorios* — could not be sourced: the
land authority page returned 404 [68].

## Regulatory instability, evidenced

Three dated instances, each from a primary source, each inside a normal hold
period:

1. **Spain struck down its own rental registry inside its second year.** RD
   1312/2024 entered force 2 January 2025 with effects from 1 July 2025 [15]; the
   Supreme Court annulled its registry articles by judgments of 19 May, 21 May and
   1 June 2026 [16]. An investor who complied in 2025 complied with a regulation
   now substantially void.
2. **Barcelona is extinguishing an entire licence class**, with all roughly
   10,000 tourist-flat licences to lapse by November 2028 under an enacted
   Catalan decree-law [17][18].
3. **Greece froze new short-let registrations in central Athens and made the
   freeze survive a sale** — transfer deletes the registry entry [25].

And one that cuts the other way on tax: **the US–Hungary income tax treaty is
terminated**, per the IRS's own verbatim caution "Hungary – CAUTION Treaty
Terminated" [50], with no date given on the page.

Read together, these say the regulatory variable in this asset class moves faster
than the hold period, and moves against the non-resident letting investor more
often than for them. That reading is a synthesis across sources; no single
fetched source characterises it as a trend.

## Panama macro — the only Investment Climate content that survived

The ITA country commercial guide [62], last published 27 March 2026, reproduces
the Panama executive summary. Named impediments to investment: "corruption,
insufficient transparency and judicial capacity, **non-payment issues**, and an
undereducated workforce". Fiscal deficit **7.4% of GDP in 2024** against a 4.0%
statutory target; debt **$56.3bn at April 2025, about 70% of GDP**; **Fitch
downgraded Panama to BB+, non-investment grade, on 28 March 2024**, with Moody's
Baa3 and S&P BBB− at 9 June 2025. Removed from the FATF Grey List in October 2023.

"Non-payment issues" and weak judicial capacity are the two that bear directly on
a landlord's ability to enforce a lease.

The equivalent Costa Rica guide is a stub containing only section headings and a
link back to the inaccessible state.gov page [63].

## Squatting and adverse possession

**Almost entirely unevidenced.** No fetched file addresses *usucapión*,
*usucapione*, *usucapião*, *prescripción adquisitiva* or *precarismo* for any of
the nine. Two partial exceptions:

- **Costa Rica**: the coastal zone is imprescriptible, so adverse possession
  cannot run there [7]. Nothing is known about inland land.
- **France**: the CNCJ briefing states plainly that "il n'existe pas de
  statistiques consolidées sur le nombre de squats", offering a third-party
  estimate of roughly 6,000–7,000 illicit occupations in 2022 and 1,130 court
  decisions in 2019 of which 93% ordered eviction — both attributed to footnotes
  whose targets were not retrieved [30]. Treat as indicative only.

Spain's *okupación* regime, the single most-cited deterrent in popular
commentary, is represented in this corpus only by a caseload count — 460
possession filings under art. 250.1.4º LEC in Q1 2026, down 22.3% [31]. No
duration, no outcome data, no statutory analysis.

## Gaps

- Expropriation record, investor-state cases, capital controls, treaty recourse:
  **all nine countries**, caused by [63] and [65].
- Judicial capacity for Costa Rica, Mexico and Panama: no instrument covers them.
- Squatting and adverse possession: **six of nine** — partial evidence exists
  only for Costa Rica (coastal imprescriptibility), France (unofficial estimates)
  and Spain (a caseload count, not a duration).
- Greece: nothing country-specific beyond EU rank orders and the short-let
  restriction.
- Whether Hungary's permit is refused in practice, or is a fee-and-delay
  formality: no approval-rate data exists.
- Whether Mexico's 50-year trust extension is granted as of right: the statute is
  permissive and no renewal-practice evidence was found.
